# Model overview

The **Non-Elective Flow Simulation** is an open-source discrete-event simulation developed by Helena Robinson at Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. It represents patients moving from the emergency department into SDEC or an inpatient bed and explores how bed capacity, admitted length of stay and SDEC activity affect queues and waiting times. The model is written in Python using SimPy and includes a Streamlit interface.

[How to join](../../join-us/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .session-join-action}

{{< include ../_all-sessions.qmd >}}

## Actions for participants before the session

- Retain the working environment and editable repository from Session 1 (if you did not attend Session 1, confirm that you can complete a model run before this session).
- Consider one assumption or feature you would change.
- Make the change to the code.
- Consider how you would test whether the change you have made has been successful.
- If time permits, test the functionality of the code.

::: {.callout-warning title="Local software requirement"}
**This model uses Python.** To run it locally, you will need Python installed and will need to install the packages specified by the repository. You can use the hosted Streamlit application without installing Python.
:::

## Getting help

If you have a problem running or reusing the Non-Elective Flow Simulation, [open an issue in the ReModel repository](https://github.com/ReModel-Club/Non-Elective-Flow-Simulation/issues). This is the best way to contact the ReModel team about the model. Describe what you were trying to do, what happened and any error messages you received.

## Session objectives and outline

This will be a discussion session around our attempts to edit and reuse the model. Participants will discuss:

- what changes they made to the repository and how they went about doing it;
- how they went about testing the change, or how they would plan to test the change they made;
- how changes should be documented and integrated with existing documentation;
- whether any changes to the repository would have made running or reusing the model easier.

The aim is for participants to leave the session with a clear understanding of how to make changes to a repository and how to test that those changes work as intended.

## Additional resources

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ReModel-Club/Non-Elective-Flow-Simulation) — source code and repository documentation.
- [Project presentation slides](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BIUDaDfDp2cj6EF19908XQ4eB7h9GMCp/view) — background to the model and its intended use.
- [HSMA showcase presentation](https://youtu.be/0DUx5hhxjoA) — recorded project presentation.
- [Vidigi paper](https://doi.org/10.1080/17477778.2026.2663849) — related work on animated visualisation of discrete-event simulation models, using this model as an application example.

The project is documented through its repository and HSMA materials. We are not currently aware of a dedicated peer-reviewed paper or independent reproduction of this specific model.
